fragments into the structure of
polydimethyldiallylammonium (PD) on through-hole copper plating
performance: A theoretical and experimental study

A B S T R A C T
In this study, SO was used to chemically modify the commonly used leveling agent poly-
dimethyldiallylammonium (PD) in through-hole electroplating, resulting in a more effective leveling agent, PDS,
which improved the throwing power (TP), leading to through-hole circuit boards with better metal coverage in
difficult-to-reach areas. Furthermore, theoretical and experimental studies were conducted to understand how
the −SO structure influences the leveling ability of the leveling agent. The study demonstrates that the −SO -
modified additive significantly enhances the copper plating process, resulting in thicker and more uniform de-
posits in through-holes, which are critical for ensuring high-quality circuit boards.Additionally, this study elu
cidates the mechanism of action of the leveling agent on the copper surface, providing theoretical support for the
development of copper plating leveling agents. The leveling ability differences between the leveling agents PD
and PDS were investigated using Cyclic Voltammetry, constant current method, and Electrochemical Impedance
Spectroscopy. Additionally, the optimal concentrations of the additives were determined. Quantum chemical
calculations were employed to analyze the electrostatic potential, HOMO/LUMO orbitals, and differential charge
density on the Cu (111) surface for both leveling agents. These theoretical analyses provided insights into the
reasons behind the differing leveling abilities of the two agents.

number of consumer products, such as computers, electronic watches,
wearable devices, smartphones, and communication equipment, are
becoming more intelligent, lightweight, and miniaturized[1–3]. In these

research on the relationship between the molecular structure of indi
vidual leveling agent molecules and their leveling performance.

the leveling agent molecule PD, analyzing the reasons behind the dif-
ferences in leveling capabilities between the PD and PDS molecules.

the

the amount of the additive increases, this polarizing effect becomes
more pronounced. Research into the effects of the two leveling agents on
the trend of anodic stripping coulombs reveals that PD does not polarize
the crystallization of copper ions as significantly as PDS. Compared to
PDS, the addition of PD results in a lesser reduction in anodic stripping
coulombs. Additionally, the saturation concentrations of the two agents
differ. Once the concentration of PDS reaches 50 mg/L, further increases
in the additive do not significantly enhance the polarizing effect, indi-
cating that the leveling action of PDS has reached its limit at this con-
centration. Even at a PD concentration of 100 mg/L, the anodic stripping
coulombs remain lower than those of PDS, indicating that its inhibitory
ability is weaker. The specific values of anodic stripping coulombs at

concentration revealed a significant reduction in porosity, indicating

plating layer. Observations from the profilometer showed that the
